item.title: Do looped transformers write reasoning they don't use?
item.description: TL;DR: Huginn uses its reasoning. More loops didn’t change that. How I got this idea What is a looped transformer Experiment Results Where each model stops needing the trace A probe that looked like a result and was not What this does and does not show How I got this idea So I was browsing HackerNews the other day and read a blog about the gpt6-astra [1] that speculated Astra may be using looped transformer logic introduced by earlier research work [2]. I like reading these since new ideas always come to my mind. This topic was somewhat familiar to me, but I was curious what is all the fuss about looped transformers hiding their reasoning traces and that they may be inferring most from their hidden states. Naturally I would search the web to try to find some research that already checked this out, but I couldn’t find any that tested exactly this (would like to see if I missed some somehow; there is just too much research going on at any given moment). The closest I found is Lu et al. [3], who looked inside Huginn with the reasoning turned off and found little sign of it reasoning in its loop. But I couldn’t find anyone who checked whether a looped model actually uses the reasoning it writes. So this post is about how I tried to verify and check this, but first let’s shortly jump in to see what the hell a looped transformer is.

item.title: An AI agent wrote the code that runs your robots. What else can that code do?
item.description: An AI agent's code sends jobs to a robot vendor with the business's password in hand. What else could it do with that password, and how do you know? A small example: the code runs in plimsoll's sandbox, a gatekeeper passes on only the requests it is allowed and adds a one-off password, every attempt to do more is refused and recorded, and the one bug no sandbox catches, a double order after a lost reply, is caught by the vendor's own ledger.
